home.title: Alpha Tester — feedback with context, from inside the app
home.description: Alpha Tester: a feedback widget for apps in testing. Reports arrive with the screen, the console and the environment; one agent triages them and opens the GitHub issue, another proposes the fix in a draft PR.

precos.title: Pricing
precos.lead: You pay for the platform monthly and for the AI by use: the model's cost plus a transparent fee, charged to your company's credits. No surprises on the invoice.

feedback.name: Feedback only
feedback.desc: Widget with context (marked element, screenshot, console errors, offline queue) and a dashboard to follow everything.
items: Packs of 100, 500 or 2,000 feedback items a month (R$ 29, R$ 79, R$ 199)

noAgent.name: No agent
noAgent.desc: Manual triage in the dashboard, status for the reporter, CLI and MCP server.
items: 1,000 feedback items a month, 5 projects, 5 seats
With GitHub: create the issue straight from the feedback, with link and labels

triage.name: Triage agent
triage.desc: The AI filters malicious content, finds duplicates, classifies, estimates the effort and opens the GitHub issue.
items: Packs of R$ 50, R$ 150 or R$ 450 (about 160, 500 or 1,550 triages)
2,000 feedback items a month, 10 projects, 10 seats

implementer.name: Implementer agent
implementer.desc: The AI reads the issue and the code, makes the change, runs the checks and opens a draft pull request for your team to review.
items: Packs of R$ 200, R$ 600 or R$ 1,800 (about 11, 36 or 112 medium-sized PRs)
Every job starts only after your approval
2,000 feedback items a month, 10 projects, 10 seats

both.name: Full loop · both agents
both.desc: From feedback to pull request: triage and implementation on the same credit wallet.
items: Packs of R$ 300, R$ 900 or R$ 2,400
5,000 feedback items a month, 20 projects, 15 seats

credits.title: How credits work
credits.text: Each agent run charges the real cost of the AI model plus a 30 % to 40 % fee, depending on the pack. The amounts above are estimates for typical runs; you follow every charge on the statement. Unused credits roll over to the next month. You set a daily limit per project, and the agent stops when the balance runs out, with no extra charge.
credits.annual: Annual billing: 2 months free on the subscription.

hero.title: the loop
hero.summary: Animation of the Alpha Tester loop: the widget sends feedback with a screenshot to the dashboard; the dashboard notifies the triage agent, which opens the GitHub issue; a person approves the implementer, which opens a draft PR; the team reviews and merges, and the new version goes back to the tester.

widget.title: Widget
cap: The tester marks a region and the report carries the screen, the console and the environment.
Public key: it only sends feedback. Offline, it waits in the browser's queue.

painel.title: Dashboard
cap: Companies, projects and members with roles; feedback with filters and history.
Screenshots in private storage. Notifies the agents with a signed webhook.

cli.title: at CLI
cap: Feedback in the terminal, with the project's secret key: list, read, triage and open issues.
Coming soon.

mcp.title: MCP server
cap: For any agent that speaks MCP: T0 reads, T1 annotates, T2 proposes.
No tool returns who reported. Coming soon.

triagem.title: Triage agent
cap: Security first: the tester's text is data, never an instruction.
Then duplicates, type and size, within the project's daily budget. Coming soon.

issue.title: GitHub issue
cap: One issue per feedback, in the project's repository, with labels.
A fine-grained token for one repository, encrypted in the dashboard.

impl.title: Implementer
cap: It starts only with an owner's or admin's approval, within a cost limit.
Shallow clone, up to three rounds, HTML and links checked. Coming soon.

pr.title: Draft PR
cap: One draft PR per job, on its own branch.
Never on the default branch, never force-pushed, never merged. Coming soon.

revisao.title: Human review
cap: Your team approves the job, reviews the diff and merges.
The reporter sees “Delivered” in the widget.

w-p.title: feedback + screenshot
cap: HTTPS with the project's public key, screenshot included.

cli-p.title: at → dashboard
cap: Secret key with the manage scope; 30 requests a minute.

mcp-p.title: MCP → dashboard
cap: Tools above the maximum tier are not even listed.

p-t.title: signed webhook
cap: Ids only: the agent reads the feedback again at the source before acting.

t-i.title: GitHub issue
cap: With the project's token; missing labels are created, existing ones are left alone.

i-m.title: accepted issue
cap: The implementer reads the size S issue, accepted and approved.

ok.title: approval
cap: The owner confirms the cost limit. Nothing else starts a job.

m-pr.title: push + draft PR
cap: Branch alpha-t/issue-N; the PR closes the issue when someone merges it.

pr-r.title: review
cap: The PR waits for your team, with the check results.

r-w.title: new version
cap: Merge and deploy are done by people; the status goes back to the reporter.

relato: The report arrives with context: screen, console and environment.
issue: One issue per feedback, with labels.
impl: A draft PR, after an approval.

log.r1: owner approves the job · limit R$ 2.00
log.x1: shallow clone of the default branch · 3.2 MB
log.r2: reviews the diff and the checks

intro.hint: each scene plays on its own · hover or tap the objects to read · Esc closes

fab.title: Feedback button
lines: A button in your web app: type (bug, improvement, suggestion), title and description.
Script tag or ESM import, with the public key at_pub_.

captura.title: Capture
lines: Mark elements, crop a region or capture the full page.
PNG, JPEG, WebP, GIF or PDF attachments, up to 5 MB.

console.title: Console
lines: Console errors, unhandled errors and rejected promises travel with the report.

ambiente.title: Environment
lines: Page, marked element and its position, browser, window size and time.

fila.title: Offline
lines: The report waits in a queue in the browser and goes out when the connection is back, without duplicates.

org.title: Companies and projects
lines: Each company has its projects; each project, members with the roles owner, admin, editor and viewer.

lista.title: Feedback
lines: Filters by status, type and priority; status changes with history and internal notes.

anexos.title: Attachments
lines: Kept in private storage, opened in the dashboard and in the issue through signed links.

chaves.title: API keys
lines: Public for the widget, secret for servers and terminals.
Shown once and revocable on the spot.

tracker.title: My feedback
lines: The reporter follows along: Submitted, Under review, In progress, Resolved, Delivered.
No login: the link lives in the browser.

seguranca.title: Security screening
lines: The tester's text is data, never an instruction.
No clean verdict, no issue.

duplicados.title: Duplicates
lines: Compares with the project's feedback and open issues, even in another language.
A repeat becomes a +1 on the original issue.

etiquetas.title: Type and size
lines: Labels alpha-t, type:… and size:…
Creates the missing ones, never changes existing ones.

orcamento.title: Budget per project
lines: A daily cap for everything the agent spends on the project, with its own encrypted key.
At the cap, feedback waits for the next day; other projects carry on.

privacidade.title: No personal data
lines: The agent never reads the reporter's name or email.

token.title: One token per project
lines: Fine-grained, limited to one repository: Metadata and Issues.
Contents and Pull requests only for the implementer; never Workflows.

cifrado.title: Stored encrypted
lines: Encrypted on save and never sent back to the browser: the dashboard shows only the last four characters.

criar.title: Create issue
lines: By hand on each feedback, or automatically when the feedback is accepted.
One issue per feedback.

corpo.title: Issue body
lines: Type, priority, page, description, attachments and environment, with the project's labels.
In a public repository, the issue is public too.

autor.title: Author
lines: Issues and PRs appear under the account that created the token; an account dedicated to automation keeps personal names out.

aprovacao.title: Approval in the dashboard
lines: Only an owner or admin starts it, on an accepted feedback that already has an issue.
Neither a label nor a schedule starts a job.

clone.title: Shallow clone
lines: Only the default branch, in a temporary folder deleted at the end; above 50 MB, no clone.
Nothing from the repository is executed.

diff.title: What may change
lines: In the first version, static content: HTML, CSS, text and images, on size S issues.
Never code, build, CI or new scripts.

verificacoes.title: Checks
lines: Valid HTML in the changed files and no broken internal links; up to three rounds.

custo.title: Cost limit
lines: Stops at the job's limit or the day's budget, whichever comes first; 15-minute deadline.
The project's own key: no key, no run.

ui.failText: comment on the issue · no PR

pr.title: Draft PR
lines: One per job, on its own branch; never on the default branch, never force-pushed.

merge.title: Merge
lines: Always your team's: Alpha Tester never merges.

falha.title: If it fails
lines: No PR; one comment on the issue with the reason, and the details only in the dashboard.

entregue.title: Delivered
lines: The reporter sees the status change in the widget.

terminal.h2Html: The at CLI and the MCP server

cli.title: at
lines: feedback list, show, set and issue.
Never prints the key, speaks HTTPS only and does not follow redirects.

chave.title: Project secret key
lines: at_sec_…, created in the dashboard by an admin, shown once, revocable on the spot.
Never in a web page or a repository.

escopos.title: Scopes
lines: ingest only sends feedback.
manage acts as a project editor and never manages keys, members or GitHub.

niveis.title: MCP tiers
lines: T0 reads, T1 annotates, T2 proposes status changes and opens the issue.
Above the maximum tier, the tool is not even listed.

auditoria.title: Audit
lines: Every write goes to a local log.
No tool returns who reported; the tester's text arrives marked as data.

fora.title: Outside Alpha Tester
lines: The public key only sends feedback; the secret one stays on servers and terminals.

cofre.title: Encrypted keys
lines: GitHub tokens and model keys encrypted (AES-256-GCM) and never sent back.
API keys stored only as a hash.

empresas.title: Data per company
lines: Every query is filtered by the key's project or by the role in the dashboard.
Nothing is shared between clients.

identidade.title: Who reports
lines: Agents and the MCP server never read or return a name or email.

limites.title: Limits
lines: Rate limits per key and two-step verification in the dashboard.

repo.title: GitHub
lines: Reached only with that project's token, limited to one repository; workflow changes stay with people.

apps.tagline: Apps distributed and tested with Alpha Tester.

cutavid.descHtml: Cut and assemble videos in seconds: watch in the built-in player, pick the segments with the dual slider, preview and export — and now watch the whole composition before exporting. Combine several segments — from one or many videos —, reorder or reverse them and save everything in a single file. Fast cut without re-encoding or frame-accurate — with ffmpeg built in, nothing else to install.
steps: Open the extracted CutAVid folder and run cutavid.exe from inside it — the files in the folder work together, do not move the .exe on its own.
Full instructions in LEIA-ME.txt inside the folder.
On the first run Windows may show “Windows protected your PC”. Click More info and then Run anyway — the warning appears because the app is not digitally signed yet.
cutavid.verifyHtml: To check, in PowerShell: Get-FileHash .\cutavid-windows-x64-v1.3.0.zip (upper or lower case does not matter).

widget.title: Alpha Tester feedback widget
widget.text: The Alpha Tester widget for apps in testing — bug reports and suggestions sent from inside the app, with screenshots and status tracking for the tester. Available for the web and, soon, for Flutter.
